title: Tamil Nadu Politics – Evening Brief – 14 November 2026
headline: DMK Urges All-Party Meet Over Mekedatu As Former Civil Servants Demand Restoration of Federal Relations Panel

sections.big_picture:
Tamil Nadu's political landscape is witnessing heightened friction between regional stakeholders and the state administration led by Chief Minister C. Joseph Vijay, centering on federal rights, inter-state water disputes, and legislative accountability. DMK President M.K. Stalin has formally demanded an all-party meeting to counter Karnataka's aggressive pursuit of the Mekedatu dam project across the Cauvery river, following provocative statements by Karnataka Deputy Chief Minister D.K. Shivakumar. Concurrently, a collective of 72 retired civil servants under the banner of the Constitutional Conduct Group has strongly criticized the state government's decision to disband the High-Level Committee on Union-State Relations, terming it a retrograde policy retreat that weakens Tamil Nadu's historic stand on fiscal federalism and regional autonomy.

Simultaneously, governance challenges have intensified across multiple administrative tiers, highlighted by legislative friction in Kallakurichi, opposition broadsides regarding law and order, and public welfare distributions. While Chief Minister Vijay inaugurated a statewide Children's Day initiative distributing cakes and sweet pongal to over 61.8 lakh students at a financial outlay of ₹9.27 crore, opposition parties including the PMK, NTK, and CPM have sharply targeted the ruling dispensation over police inaction, administrative misconduct, and inadequate statutory fund utilization. Legal and judicial interventions continue to check executive inertia, exemplified by Madras High Court directives probing medical negligence and mandating strict accountability across state apparatuses.

sections.government_and_administration: - **Chief Minister Vijay Launches Children’s Day Welfare Distribution Worth ₹9.27 Crore:** Tamil Nadu Chief Minister C. Joseph Vijay inaugurated a first-of-its-kind state welfare initiative on Friday, distributing cakes, greeting cards, and sweet pongal to school students and anganwadi children across the state. A total of 61,84,566 beneficiaries—encompassing students, teachers, and non-teaching staff in government and government-aided primary, middle, high, and higher secondary institutions—received the festive items funded through an official allocation of ₹9.27 crore. Meanwhile, administrative transparency faced sharp scrutiny as the Tribal Liberation Movement petitioned the government to ensure 100% utilization of the ₹20,365.64 crore allocated under the Scheduled Caste Sub-Plan (SCSP) and ₹1,879.09 crore earmarked under the Tribal Sub-Plan (TSP) for the 2025-26 fiscal period. State coordinator V. Agathiyan stressed that comprehensive fund deployment is vital for mitigating systemic socio-economic disparities plaguing marginalized communities. Concurrently, anti-corruption proceedings advanced as former DMK minister E.V. Velu appeared before the Directorate of Vigilance and Anti-Corruption (DVAC) in Tiruvannamalai regarding an alleged illegal soil excavation scam involving the unauthorized mining of 8.22 crore rupees worth of earth from the Malapampadi Lake. ([The Hindu](https://www.thehindu.com/news/national/tamil-nadu/tn-cm-vijay-launches-distribution-of-cakes-greeting-cards-sweet-pongal-to-school-students-for-childrens-day/article71697560.ece))
sections.political_parties_and_opposition: - **Opposition Parties Blast Ruling TVK Regime Over Lawlessness, Police Misconduct, and Missing Persons:** Opposition leaders mounted scathing attacks on the ruling TVK administration over deteriorating law enforcement and administrative impunity. MDMK principal secretary Durai Vaiko claimed that despite NCRB data showing 1,300 murders between 2022 and 2026, crime has marginally stabilized under current governance, though political interference in local offences remains a concern. NTK chief Seeman launched a virulent tirade against Chief Minister C. Joseph Vijay, labeling him a 'reels hero' lacking the political courage to penalize erring lawmakers, including the Deputy Speaker who allegedly assaulted a civilian and a Kallakurichi MLA linked to offensive messages targeting a district collector. This controversy deepened as former TNCC chief K. Selvaperunthagai publicly clashed with incumbent Manickam Tagore over softening stances toward the accused legislator. In Villupuram, DMK deputy general secretary Kanimozhi visited the grieving parents of seven-year-old Hemalatha, who has remained missing for 33 days from Gingee without police breakthrough. Additionally, the CPM petitioned the DGP alleging local police connivance in framing anti-Tasmac activist Rajkumar with planted contraband in Sivaganga district. ([DT Next](https://www.dtnext.in/news/tamilnadu/reels-hero-lacks-guts-to-act-erring-mlas-says-seeman-2))
sections.assembly_courts_and_policy: - **Madras High Court Mandates Medical Council Probe Into 12-Year Surgical Needle Retention; PMK Moves Court on Tamil Language:** In a harrowing case of medical negligence, the Madras High Court ordered a comprehensive Tamil Nadu Medical Council inquiry after it was revealed that a surgical needle had been left inside a woman’s abdomen for 12 years following an operation. The bench emphasized strict accountability for institutional negligence, directing medical authorities to submit a detailed compliance report. In a separate legal development, the PMK filed a public interest litigation (PIL) before the High Court seeking a mandatory writ directing the state government to formally transmit long-pending Assembly resolutions—passed unanimously in 2006 and 2026—to the Union government for Presidential assent to make Tamil the official language of the Madras High Court. PMK general secretary Vadivel Ravanan argued in the petition that introducing Tamil as a court language is essential to guarantee judicial access for rural litigants and backward-class advocates. Meanwhile, the High Court also intervened in administrative failures by transferring the high-profile Isha Yoga Centre missing person investigation directly to the CB-CID following local police inaction. ([Live Law](https://news.google.com/rss/articles/CBMivgFBVV95cUxNVmF1SmRCUWN4bHFQaFpUeGQyUEoxUVhUVzRSSHluTGFBOXBDY2hIcUtJaVNNd184RUJkRTJCV2ppNTlHX29qMXJvRE11SmY3eS1LeE5GQnItNzNIQWdtTGR4T2o1Z29NUVRwanUyWTVpNFh2V3BjeGRINnJ2T3M1MjFhR1JPZlQtVVh6VF9xZ1EwSjBmSVdEMDRmT0ZCeFhtX0U1TV90ZmR6TUxOWDh4Y0J0a1pSNXROYmw1d0ZR0gG-AUFVX3lxTE1WYXVKZEJRY3hscVBoWlR4ZDJQSjFRWFRXNFJIeW5MYUE5cENjaEhxS0lpU013XzhFQmRFMkJXamk1OUdfb2oxcm9ETXVKZjd5LUt4TkZCci03M0hBZ21MZHhPajVnb01RVHBqdTJZNWk0WHZXcGN4ZEg2cnZPczUyMWFHUk9mVC1VWHpUX3FnUTBKMGZJV0QwNGZPRkJ4WG1fRTVNX3RmZHpNTE5YOHhjQnRrWlI1dE5ibDV3RlE?oc=5))
sections.district_developments: - **Administrative Crises and Protests Grip Districts from Villupuram to Tiruvannamalai:** Local governance across Tamil Nadu experienced acute strain as district administrations grappled with public agitations, unsolved abductions, and environmental exploitation probes. In Villupuram district, the 33-day disappearance of seven-year-old Hemalatha from Alampoondi village near Gingee triggered widespread public outrage, culminating in high-profile political visits by opposition leaders demanding intensified combing operations by local police forces. In Sivaganga and Tirupathur taluks, rural tensions escalated after the CPM accused prohibition wing personnel of colluding with Tasmac bar operators to plant ganja and frame local anti-liquor activist Rajkumar, who has spearheaded peaceful demonstrations demanding the shuttering of liquor outlets near educational institutions. Concurrently, in Tiruvannamalai, state vigilance authorities intensified inquiries into illegal soil excavation, summoning former minister E.V. Velu to answer charges regarding the illicit mining of over eight crore rupees worth of earth from the Malapampadi Lake ecosystem. These district-level flashpoints highlight mounting friction between grassroots activists, local law enforcement, and regional administrative machinery. ([DT Next](https://www.dtnext.in/news/tamilnadu/33-days-but-no-trace-of-missing-senji-girl-kanimozhi-visits-parents))
sections.what_to_watch_next: Over the next 24 to 48 hours, political observers and policymakers will closely monitor potential announcements regarding an all-party meeting on the Mekedatu dam dispute, as opposition pressure mounts on Chief Minister C. Joseph Vijay to challenge Karnataka's unilateral moves. Legal circles will track upcoming Madras High Court hearings regarding the CB-CID probe transfer in the Isha Yoga Centre missing person case and responses from the state government on the PMK's PIL seeking Tamil as the official High Court language. Additionally, civil society groups are expected to announce statewide protests if the state government fails to clarify its stance on restoring the disbanded High-Level Committee on Union-State Relations and the full allocation of SCSP/TSP budgetary funds.
